channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Additive Effects of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Robotic Therapy for Upper Extremity Recovery After Chronic Ischemic Stroke: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Sham-Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (N=36) found that adding repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) or transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to robotic therapy did not provide additional benefits for upper extremity motor and functional recovery in patients with chronic ischemic stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Dizziness, Balance, and Postural Stability in Adult Patients With Chronic Peripheral Vestibular Dizziness.
item.description: A double-blind RCT with 56 adults with chronic vestibular dizziness found that repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with vestibular rehabilitation (VR) significantly improved dizziness, balance, and postural stability over 8 weeks compared to sham stimulation + VR.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of sportsmetrics training on biomechanical and functional performance outcomes related to ACL injury risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis confirmed the positive effects of SportsMetrics training on ACL injury-related biomechanical deficits and functional performance outcomes in athletes.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Physical and mental health-related quality of life outcomes of non-pharmacological interventions in early multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found effects of non-pharmacological interventions on physical and mental health-related quality of life among adults with early diagnosed multiple sclerosis, with findings pooled using standardized mean differences.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 articles explored the effectiveness of physical exercise on cognitive function and optimal dosage in older adults with Alzheimer's disease, drawing from Embase, PsycInfo, and Ovid Medline databases.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Bidirectional association between injuries and mental health symptoms among elite athletes: a systematic review
item.description: A systematic review of 25 studies found a bidirectional association between musculoskeletal injuries and mental health symptoms among elite athletes, indicating that mental health symptoms can precede injury, and injury can lead to subsequent mental health symptoms.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Clinically interpretable prediction models of stroke functional outcomes: A national cohort study of adults in inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the US.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study (n=43,745) developed clinically interpretable prediction models for self-care and mobility function at discharge from US inpatient rehabilitation facilities for adults with stroke, using only Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Patient Assessment Instrument (IRF-PAI) variables.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=50) demonstrated that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis in patients with limb oedema compared to 0% tension taping by day 9, with effects sustained to day 16.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual reality-assisted rehabilitation after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair for small-to-medium supraspinatus tears: a prospective assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial
item.description: A prospective assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial examined virtual reality-assisted rehabilitation after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair for small-to-medium supraspinatus tears, noting VR's potential to standardize tasks and provide feedback.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Slow eccentric- versus concentric-focused resistance training in middle-aged and older women with knee osteoarthritis: A randomized trial
item.description: A randomized trial compared the short-term effects of slow eccentric-only resistance training (SET) and slow concentric-only resistance training (SCT) on pain and physical function in middle-aged and older women with knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Nordic walking and sprinting enhance lower limb vertical power in Parkinson’s: an exploratory study
item.description: An exploratory study found that Nordic walking and sprinting enhanced lower limb vertical power, specifically jump height and peak power, in individuals with Parkinson's disease.
item.author: Sport Sci Health

item.title: Mental health in elite athletes: International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026)
item.description: The updated International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026) emphasizes that mental health symptoms and disorders are common in elite athletes, may be sport-related, and impact performance, recommending routine screening and monitoring.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Short-term inspiratory muscle training, aerobic exercise, and detraining in women with COPD: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial in women with COPD found that short-term inspiratory muscle training (IMT), aerobic exercise (AE), and combined IMT+AE all significantly improved inspiratory muscle strength, exercise capacity, and quality of life, with effects diminishing after a detraining period.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Managing Patients With Hypermobility Disorders: They've Seen You, but Have You Seen Them?
item.description: This editorial addresses the challenges physical therapists face in managing patients with hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS), advocating for a shift from fragmented, passive care to comprehensive strategies guided by international classification updates and emerging consensus.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Danish Guideline Treatments for Breast Cancer and Physiotherapy-Relevant Late Effects: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
item.description: A nationwide Danish cohort study investigated the association between guideline-based breast cancer treatments and the risk of self-reported shoulder impairment, lymphedema, and fatigue 3-7 years post-surgery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Pregnancy-Related Musculoskeletal Pain: Current Management, Influence on Biopsychosocial Health, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction With Care.
item.description: An international internet survey with 671 female respondents investigated the prevalence of musculoskeletal pain during pregnancy, its impact on biopsychosocial well-being, healthcare pain management, and its influence on satisfaction with prenatal care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Telerehabilitation before and after lumbar spine surgery: A scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review mapped existing evidence on telerehabilitation interventions for patients undergoing lumbar spine surgery, focusing on intervention characteristics and identifying evidence gaps.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: External validation of the minimal important change in the Berg Balance Scale scores of patients hospitalized for subacute stroke.
item.description: A longitudinal study (n=286) investigated the external validation of several reported minimal important change (MIC) values in the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) scores for patients with subacute stroke in a rehabilitation unit.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of opioid-free intraoperative anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative immune function in elderly patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty: a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial
item.description: A single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial investigates the effects of opioid-free intraoperative anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative immune function in elderly patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Associations between patient quality of life and caregiver burden among older adults receiving comprehensive geriatric assessment via telemedicine: a cross-sectional study from Seha Virtual Hospital, Saudi Arabia
item.description: A cross-sectional study from Saudi Arabia explores associations between patient quality of life and caregiver burden among older adults receiving comprehensive geriatric assessment via telemedicine.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics
